sections.h2: What should a Wall Township homeowner know before selling quickly?
sections.html:
Wall Township sits close to the Jersey Shore with highway and rail access, yet a quick sale still depends on the township's occupancy rules, the state's closing fees and the condition of the house. With a Census median home value above $700,000, the percentage-based charges at closing deserve a close look.

Owners choose between hiring an agent, handling the sale alone, and signing with a buyer who pays cash. The sections below cover local facts behind each choice.

sections.h2: Where is Wall Township and what shapes its housing market?
sections.html:
Wall covers 30.66 square miles of land plus 1.03 square miles of water in eastern Monmouth County. The legislature formed it as a township in 1851, and later pieces of its territory became Spring Lake, Sea Girt, Manasquan, Brielle, Belmar and other shore boroughs. What remains is a large, mostly suburban township with the census-designated places of Allenwood and West Belmar, plus neighborhoods such as Glendola, Old Mill, Allaire and Remsen Mills.

Wreck Pond, a tidal pond on the Atlantic coast, lies on the township's edge with Spring Lake, Spring Lake Heights and Sea Girt, and its watershed covers about 12 square miles. Allaire State Park and the Edgar Felix Bikeway run through the township, and the Brick Township Reservoir, shared with Brick, has a 1.7-mile trail. If your lot is near a pond or tidal stream, ask your surveyor or insurer whether it falls in a mapped flood zone, since buyers will ask.

Allaire Village began as an iron-making community in 1822 and later became part of Allaire State Park. The township grew from 7,386 residents in 1950 to 16,498 in 1970 and 25,261 in 2000. The Census Bureau's July 1, 2025 estimate is 26,753, only slightly above the 2020 count of 26,525, which points to a settled housing stock.

sections.h2: How do Wall's roads and rail lines affect a home sale?
sections.html:
Wall is a transportation crossroads for central New Jersey. The Garden State Parkway has an interchange here (exit 98, Belmar and Wall), Interstate 195 ends at Route 34, and Routes 18, 33, 34, 35, 70 and 71 all pass through. Commuters can use the Monmouth Park and Ride at Parkway mile marker 100 for express buses to Manhattan, while NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line serves the area from stations at Belmar, Manasquan and Spring Lake.

Most of the road network is township-maintained, so a street's plowing and repair schedule is a question for the township. Monmouth Executive Airport is also inside the township, and the largest nearby hospital, Jersey Shore University Medical Center, is in neighboring Neptune Township.

sections.h2: What does Census data show about Wall homeowners?
sections.html:
About 83 in 100 Wall homes are lived in by their owners (83.4% for 2020 to 2024). The median owner-occupied home is valued at $720,400, and owners report median monthly costs of $3,162 with a mortgage and $1,378 without. Median household income is $142,768.

Residents 65 or older make up 22.8% of the population, and 93.0% of people stayed put for the previous year. Long ownership often ends in a downsize, an inheritance or a relocation, and the next sections cover the paperwork.

Wall Township Public Schools run from pre-kindergarten through grade 12. The 2024-25 enrollment was 3,215 students across seven schools: Wall Primary, Allenwood, Central, Old Mill and West Belmar elementary schools, Wall Intermediate School (grades 6 to 8, 755 students) and Wall High School (924 students). The district reported a student-teacher ratio of 9.3 to 1.

One district covers every grade, so learn which elementary school serves your address before listing.

sections.h2: What does the township require before a Wall house is sold?
sections.html:
The Wall Building Department enforces the state Uniform Construction Code and issues a certificate of occupancy or approval once final inspections pass. The office is at 2700 Allaire Road, phone 732-449-8444, extension 2225. The Land Use Office reviews residential zoning permit applications.

Ask both offices whether your sale needs a resale or transfer approval, what it costs, and what permits the property has on file. Fire inspections for the whole township come from the Fire Prevention Bureau, which also has an office at 2700 Allaire Road.

  • Before a one- or two-family house changes hands, the state wants smoke alarms with sealed ten-year batteries on the walls.
  • Open or expired permits for decks, finished basements or additions are the usual cause of closing delays.
  • Ask the township who inspects a private well or septic system, and what the buyer's lender will require.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees come with a Wall Township sale?
sections.html:
At a median value over $700,000, many Wall sales land in the upper rows of the state's Realty Transfer Fee chart, which shows $5.30 per $500 for the slice from $550,000 to $850,000. A residential deed over $1,000,000 also carries the seller's Graduated Percent Fee: 1% of the price up to $2,000,000, then 2%, then more, reaching 3.5% beyond $3,500,000. Form RTF-1EE goes with that deed.

Every owner completes a GIT/REP form. Remaining in New Jersey means GIT/REP-3. Leaving the state can mean prepaying 2% of the price or 8.97% of the gain, whichever applies. A house you owned and lived in for two of the past five years may qualify for a federal exclusion of some or all of the gain. Your closing attorney will confirm the numbers before you sign.

sections.h2: How do Wall assessments and tax appeals work?
sections.html:
Monmouth County follows the alternative calendar, so an assessment appeal is due January 15, not April 1. The county board sits at the Hall of Records in Freehold (1 East Main Street, 732-431-7404). Assessments above $1,000,000 can skip the county board. Wall's township site offers an online page for tax account lookup and payment.

The board expects evidence such as comparable sales. A leaving seller gains little from a win, while a buyer or an heir keeping the house might.

sections.h2: What local landmarks and history do Wall buyers notice?
sections.html:
Wall's character comes from its shore-adjacent geography and a few well-known sites. Allaire Village, founded as an iron works in 1822, is a living-history museum inside Allaire State Park, and the Old Wall Historical Society keeps the Allgor-Barkalow Homestead of 1840 as a museum. Camp Evans began as a Marconi wireless receiving site around 1900, and Wall Stadium, open since 1950, still hosts racing.

Wall is also a landing point for several transatlantic subsea cables, and about 68 sworn officers staff the township police department from headquarters on Allaire Road. Three fire districts and three first aid squads cover the township, so ask the Fire Prevention Bureau which district your address falls in.

faqs.q: How soon could a Wall house sale close?
faqs.a: A cash sale can close in a few weeks, while a listed sale often takes a couple of months once showings, the buyer's loan and township inspections are counted. Call the Wall Building Department early to learn its timing.

faqs.q: When must a Wall tax assessment appeal be filed?
faqs.a: By January 15, since Monmouth County uses the alternative assessment calendar. File with the Monmouth County Board of Taxation in Freehold, or call 732-431-7404.

faqs.q: What does a typical Wall home cost to own each month?
faqs.a: Census figures for 2020 to 2024 show median owner costs of $3,162 with a mortgage and $1,378 without. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $720,400, and 83.4% of homes are owner-occupied.

faqs.q: Which highways and train lines serve Wall?
faqs.a: The Garden State Parkway has an interchange here and Interstate 195 ends at Route 34. NJ Transit's North Jersey Coast Line stops at Belmar, Manasquan and Spring Lake.

faqs.q: Which fire district covers my Wall address?
faqs.a: Wall has three fire districts: West Belmar (District 1), Glendola (District 2) and South Wall (District 3). Fire inspections for sales come from the township's Fire Prevention Bureau at 2700 Allaire Road.
